comment: THE SNAPSHOT CONTRACT -- one derivation site for the payload the generator writes and the dashboard reads. packages/snapshot/src/codec.ts builds its encoder and decoder from wardColumns and facilityColumns AT MODULE LOAD, so neither the generator nor the dashboard contains a column list of its own. Landed in Stage 0 rather than Stage 1 because it depends on nothing in Stage 1 and it is the artefact whose late decision forces rework on both sides at once. Paths here are unbackticked where they name something a later stage builds.
why_pollCadenceSeconds_is_here: RELEASE GATE 2's latency clause, restated 2026-09-10, asserts that 'a client poll at the snapshot's own cadence reflects the new count'. The assertion is written against THIS CONSTANT, never against a wall-clock number in prose. 30 matches the CDN's s-maxage=30: polling faster asks the edge for a document it is contractually allowed to keep serving, so it buys nothing and costs requests. A poll may still legitimately receive a payload about 120 seconds old -- the generator's 60-second cadence, plus this cache's 30-second TTL, plus this 30-second poll interval -- which is why the original 'within 60 seconds' clause could not be met by this architecture and was restated rather than kept. CORRECTED 2026-09-21 (R-2026-09-21-43): this read 'stale-while-revalidate=300 means a poll may still legitimately receive a payload up to five minutes old'. stale-while-revalidate is DOCUMENTED as unsupported by cache.put and cache.match, and the zone does not cache this path at all, so no stale copy is ever served from the edge. The conclusion is unchanged; the bound is roughly half what was claimed. ONE SOURCE: the constant is not also carried in the envelope, because a client that could disagree with the fixture is a second derivation site.

freshnessBands.status: PROVISIONAL -- clinician confirmation pending (R-2026-09-23-67 A4, A7). These are Cowork's clinical-review PROPOSALS, not facts. Only a founder ruling on the clinicians' answer removes this label.
freshnessBands.comment: THE ONE SETTING for how old a count may be before the public page says so (R-2026-09-23-67 A4). Under 30 minutes a count is FRESH ("updated 4 min ago"); 30 minutes to 2 hours it is AGEING ("last reported 45 min ago -- call to confirm"); from 2 hours it is STALE and its age is an absolute Lagos time; from 12 hours there is NO RECENT REPORT and the count is withdrawn to small print. The page raises a banner when the snapshot ITSELF is 3 minutes old or more. An age exactly on a boundary falls into the OLDER band -- the conservative direction. Restated 2026-09-23 from 60 minutes / 2 hours / 24 hours (Release gate 3 and the v1 Bundle 4 spec), which nothing had yet rendered.
freshnessBands.why_here: Named constants, for the same reason pollCadenceSeconds is: a test asserting against 60 or 120 or 24 is asserting a number in prose, and the number in prose and the number in the code drift apart silently. FRESHNESS MAY REORDER RESULTS AND MAY NEVER FILTER THEM -- at 4am every ward is stale, so a freshness filter empties the entire result set at exactly the hour the tool matters most. Suppression at 24h removes the COUNT, never the row: the facility and its phone number stay.

decisions.v_is_never_a_timestamp_aggregate: v is a monotonic run counter or a content hash. NEVER max(updated_at) or any aggregate over it. Migration 008 writes public.ward_public.updated_at = ws.updated_at, which is correct -- a duty-flag flip changes the DERIVED gate without changing the ward's own claim -- but it means a version derived from a timestamp aggregate WOULD NOT MOVE when an anaesthetist goes off duty. The snapshot would then keep publishing a theatre as open at exactly the moment the gate closed it. Recorded here as well as in the function because this is the file both sides read.
decisions.the_serve_time_is_the_freshness_anchor: The server stamps updated_at and generated_at; the Pages Function stamps x-openbed-served-at on every response it returns. The client computes a ward's age as served_at - updated_at, and the snapshot's as served_at - generated_at, each plus monotonic elapsed time since the fetch. It NEVER reads a wall clock -- finding F3. A handset three hours fast is the case: it renders a fresh ward as a day old, or a day-old ward as fresh, with total confidence and no error anywhere. RESTATED 2026-09-23 (R-2026-09-23-67 A3) from "server_now is the only freshness anchor": server_now is written at GENERATION, so a stalled job served from cache would never age against it; the serve-time header advances while the snapshot does not.
decisions.the_snapshot_never_carries_duty_flags: Not anaesthetist, not obstetrician, not paediatrician, in any form. gated_by is the public reason and it is all the public gets. TWO REASONS, and the second is the one that will bite. First, a duty flag is a fact about a named individual's shift and the public has no business with it. Second, the F2 ESLint rule matches on IDENTIFIER NAMES -- /anaesthetist|obstetrician|paediatrician/i -- and this payload is arrays-of-arrays, which destroys names. `!f[3]` is invisible to that rule. Exposure is zero today because the payload carries only gated_by; the natural widening, 'show WHY it is closed in a tooltip', is exactly what reintroduces it, past a guard that can no longer see it. Written down because it is currently a property nobody had stated.
decisions.freshness_does_not_live_in_the_gate_pack: packages/gate has a specific identity: rules implemented TWICE, in SQL and TypeScript, pinned by a shared fixture in one test.each block. Freshness has exactly one derivation site by design -- the server never computes an age. Putting it in packages/gate invites the next contributor to write the SQL twin for symmetry, and the SQL twin of a freshness rule is `where updated_at > now() - interval '2 hours'`, which is the precise collapse scripts/lint_no_updated_at_filter.sh exists to ban.
